gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Fn key on a third-party mechanical board is not Apple's Fn/Globe key: QMK's own documentation says macOS only recognizes it when the keyboard's VID and PID match a real Apple keyboard.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com (low-profile), techwisereviews.com, mechkeyfoundry.com (Air75 V3 vs Flow 2 vs K3 Max) and enzosoler.com, all opened 2026-11-21. None mentions the Globe key or Apple Fn, and none names a browser for VIA, Keychron Launcher or NuPhyIO; they stop at 'VIA support', 'browser-based' or 'native Mac layout'. The two RTINGS pages, including the one ChatGPT cited, returned only navigation to my fetch, so I could not check their body text; that is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: It does not move the pick between the Lofree Flow 2 84 for Mac, Keychron K3 Max and NuPhy Air75 V3, because I found no source showing any of them sends Apple's Fn. It changes what the page should promise: macOS shortcuts built on Fn (Fn-E, Fn-Q, Fn-D, Fn-arrows) cannot be assumed on these boards, and Apple lists a non-Fn alternative for only some of them. The remapping point is narrower: Digital Trends describes VIA on the Flow 2 as a browser interface, while Logitech's Options+ is described by Logitech as available on macOS, which supports the MX Mechanical Mini for Mac in the 'least setup' segment only. The Safari half of the argument is not fully sourced (see unsourced).
candidates: Logitech MX Mechanical Mini for Mac

findings.label: Why a third-party board's Fn key is not Apple's Fn/Globe key
findings.value: QMK: "Unlike most Fn keys, the one on Apple keyboards actually has its own keycode... sort of." "It takes the place of the sixth keycode in a basic 6KRO HID report -- so an Apple keyboard is in fact only 5KRO." "Even worse, it is not recognized unless the keyboard's VID and PID match that of a real Apple keyboard."
findings.note: Project's own words. It applies to the Keychron K3 Max only on the basis that its product name, as shown in ChatGPT's card, says QMK/VIA; Keychron's page returned HTTP 429 so I did not confirm it there.

findings.label: QMK's position on supporting Apple Fn
findings.value: "It is technically possible to get QMK to send this key." "However, doing so requires modification of the report format to add the state of the Fn key." "The legal issues that official QMK support for this feature may create mean it is unlikely to happen."
findings.note: Explains why stock QMK boards handle Fn inside the keyboard as a layer key.

findings.label: macOS shortcuts that need Apple's Fn key
findings.value: Fn-Q Quick Note; Fn-A Dock; Fn-C Control Center; Fn-D dictation; Fn-N Notification Center; Fn-Shift-A Apps (macOS Tahoe 26 or later); Fn-Fn Character Viewer; Fn-Delete forward delete; Fn-Up/Down Page Up/Down; Fn-Left/Right Home/End. Non-Fn alternatives Apple gives: "Control–Command–Space bar or Fn-E" (Character Viewer), "Command–Mission Control or Fn-H or Fn-F11" (show desktop).
findings.note: Apple's page is dated September 14, 2026. A board whose Fn never reaches macOS can only reproduce Page Up/Down, Home/End and forward delete from its own firmware layer, if the maker mapped them.

findings.label: VIA remapping and the Fn key, per Digital Trends (Paulo Vargas)
findings.value: "The Flow 2 supports VIA, which lets you remap keys and configure different layers through a browser interface." Vargas reports VIA did not recognize the board until he got a JSON file from Lofree, and that the Fn key cannot be remapped in VIA.
findings.source_title: The Lofree Flow 2 review - Digital Trends
findings.note: Published August 9, 2026. He mainly used the Mac version. Only the first sentence is a verbatim quote; the JSON and Fn points are the fetch tool's paraphrase of his review. He does not name the browser.

findings.label: Out-of-box behaviour on a Mac, per MacSources (Nicholas Calderone)
findings.value: "What stood out most is that the keyboard was clearly designed with macOS in mind." "Right out of the box, everything worked the way I expected."
findings.note: Published January 26, 2026. The review does not say whether it was the for-Mac variant, and does not mention the Fn or Globe key or how VIA was set up.

A search snippet mentioned a 'Lofree Flow 2 Mac VIA Configurator' download, which I did not open.

Whether the Lofree Flow 2 84 for Mac, Keychron K3 Max, NuPhy Air75 V3 or Logitech MX Mechanical Mini for Mac sends Apple's Fn/Globe usage to macOS: no maker page, manual or named reviewer I opened says either way.

A page stating that VIA's web app, Keychron Launcher and NuPhyIO 2.0 use WebHID and so need Chrome, Edge or Opera instead of Safari: Keychron's software article came back truncated, nuphy.com and pay.nuphy.com returned HTTP 429, and I did not open usevia.app. A search snippet attributed 'latest Chrome, Opera, or Edge' to Keychron's blog.
Keychron K3 Max and NuPhy Air75 V3 maker pages (Mac/Win switch wording, firmware, whether remapping needs a cable, today's price): both stores returned HTTP 429.
The body text of the two RTINGS pages (best low-profile, best for Mac): the fetch returned only navigation, so I could not check whether RTINGS covers the Globe key or browser requirements.
Whether the Flow 2 runs QMK firmware (as opposed to only speaking the VIA protocol), which decides whether the QMK Apple Fn statement applies to it directly.
